test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT true about ungrouped frequency distribution?

options.text: Frequency of an observation is the number of times it occurs
Tally marks are used for finding frequencies
Used for putting raw data in a condensed form
Used when number of observations in data set is very large

solution:
**The Correct answer:** ** Used when number of observations in data set is very large**

__**Explanation:**__
An **ungrouped frequency distribution** is used when the data set is **small or manageable**. Each individual observation is listed separately with its frequency.

**Other options (why they are true):**

 
• 
 
 Frequency = number of times an observation occurs

 
 
• 
 
Tally marks are commonly used to count frequencies

 
 
• 
 
 It helps arrange raw data in a **condensed and systematic form**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** When the number of observations is **very large**, we use a **grouped frequency distribution**, not an ungrouped one.
